stimulus.text:
| Society | Environment | Main way of getting food | Settlement |
| Pueblo peoples | Arid Southwest | Dry farming of maize, beans, and squash | Permanent adobe villages |
| Iroquois villagers | Northeast woodlands | Three sisters farming, with hunting and fishing | Permanent villages |
| Chinook peoples | Rainy Pacific coast | Fishing, hunting, and foraging | Permanent villages with marked social ranks |
| Great Plains peoples | Grasslands | Bison hunting on foot, with some farming in river valleys | Mobile camps for much of the year |
| Great Basin peoples | Arid basin between mountain ranges | Hunting and gathering, moving with the seasons | Mobile camps |
stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the grounding books; see grounding.

stem: Historians describe a basic divide: where maize farming supported dense populations, life was settled and hierarchical; where it did not, life stayed smaller and more mobile. Which group best represents the 'smaller and more mobile' side of this divide?

options.text: The Mexica of the great lake city of Tenochtitlan in central Mexico.
options.misconception: Names the settled, hierarchical side, not the mobile side.

options.text: Foraging bands living in regions where maize agriculture was not practiced.
The Inca peoples of the high Andes with their terrace farms.
options.misconception: Names an empire built on intensive terrace farming.

options.text: The chiefdoms of the great Mississippian culture in the river valleys.
options.misconception: Names settled, hierarchical chiefdoms, not mobile bands.

rationales.A: Tenochtitlan held hundreds of thousands of people, which is the settled, hierarchical side of the divide.
rationales.B: Non-farming foragers match the smaller and more mobile description exactly.
rationales.C: The Inca ran a vast, organized empire on intensive farming, not a small mobile life.
rationales.D: Mississippian chiefdoms were settled and hierarchical, not smaller and more mobile.
rationales.general:
1. Name the divide. Farming regions grew settled and hierarchical, and regions without farming stayed smaller and mobile.
2. Sort the options into two piles. The Mexica, the Inca, and the Mississippians all farmed intensively, so they land in the settled pile.
3. Find the other pile. Foraging bands lived where farming was not practiced.
4. Match the description. Smaller and more mobile fits the foragers, not the farmers.
Remember: when a question gives you two sides, sort every option onto one side or the other.
